info.name: YouTube Transcripts & Research — YouTube Transcript API
info.description:
YouTube Transcripts & Research uses the Wicked YouTube Transcript Scraper API.

Retrieve existing captions from supplied public YouTube videos as text and timestamped segments, with optional source video facts and SRT/WebVTT. Up to 250 video URLs or IDs per Apify Actor run; caption availability and failures affect delivery. Read diagnostics and all delivered rows. Apify pricing per 1,000 delivered transcripts: Free/Starter $3, Scale $2.70, Business $2.40. Each started run also incurs the automatic apify-actor-start charge of $0.00005 multiplied by allocated RAM in GB, with a 1 GB minimum. Failed runs and language-only checks may incur that start charge; no delivered-transcript fee applies without a delivered transcript. For 250 delivered transcripts in one run using at most 1 GB, event charges total $0.75005 on Free/Starter, $0.67505 on Scale, or $0.60005 on Business. More allocated RAM or additional starts increase the start charge. Review current Apify pricing before running. SRT/WebVTT adds no separate result event fee. No audio transcription or translation.

Set apify_token locally to your own Apify API token. The collection sends Authorization: Bearer {{apify_token}}; all token defaults and saved run/storage identifiers are blank. Never commit credentials.

Send an explicitly authorized positive maxTotalChargeUsd on every paid start; the examples use $0.01, timeout=300 seconds and memory=4096 MB (4 GB). The native provider parameters are optional; omission uses provider/Actor settings rather than the example values. This per-run setting is not an account-wide or all-services budget: other runs, model/automation charges and later storage/API usage are separate. Do not treat it as a guaranteed all-in invoice ceiling or a refund for a failed run. At 4096 MB the Actor-start event is four units ($0.0002); it may apply even when no transcript is delivered. A $0.01 example budget may stop a larger batch before every requested video is delivered.

Prefer the asynchronous start when you need a durable run ID. Retain data.id, data.defaultDatasetId and data.defaultKeyValueStoreId from its response. A start acknowledgement is not successful delivery. Read the existing run until it is terminal, then reconcile OUTPUT diagnostics and all dataset pages. A synchronous connection can time out or disconnect after a run has started; inspect that existing run in Apify rather than automatically repeating a paid POST. Read-only requests below do not start another Actor; normal provider storage/API usage can still apply.

The first four POST requests are paid alternatives, not a sequence: choose one authorized start once. Do not run this entire collection with a runner. For a recoverable flow, choose the asynchronous start and copy data.id, data.defaultDatasetId and data.defaultKeyValueStoreId into run_id, dataset_id and key_value_store_id. Then use only the three GET requests to check status and read saved output/pages. No request scripts start work, poll automatically, or retry paid requests.

item.name: Read an existing run status (no new Actor start)

request.description: Set run_id to data.id from the already-started run. READY/RUNNING are not completion. Recheck this same GET with backoff until terminal; keep the returned defaultDatasetId/defaultKeyValueStoreId. Never repeat a paid start merely to check progress. Normal provider usage can apply.

item.name: Read saved OUTPUT diagnostics or language listing

request.description: Use the existing run's data.defaultKeyValueStoreId. Returns the raw JSON OUTPUT record, including language-only results or batch delivered/failed diagnostics. This request does not start extraction or produce a new transcript event. Normal provider storage/API usage can apply.

item.name: Read saved transcript rows (page 1; reuse dataset ID)

request.description: Use the existing run's data.defaultDatasetId. Start at offset=0 and limit=20, then advance offset by the rows returned until all saved rows are read. Use clean=false for unfiltered row counts; clean=true can omit rows. Reconcile all delivered IDs and failures with OUTPUT. This GET never starts a replacement run. Normal provider storage/API usage can apply.
